articles.title: 完形填空 · 跨部门增长团队如何突破业务增长瓶颈
articles.context: 文章以 BitTorrent 的案例说明，小企业要突破增长瓶颈，需要建立跨部门增长团队，以不同专业视角协作发现问题，并由强有力的负责人统一目标、排除干扰。
rows: Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice profit, you need to find a way to take it to the next level.
这是当下许多创业者都会遇到的常见情形：你是一家小企业的首席执行官，虽然已经获得了不错的利润，却仍需要找到办法让公司更上一层楼。
advance
What you need to do is prioritize growth by establishing a growth team.
你需要做的是把增长置于优先位置，并组建一支增长团队。
emphasize
A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus exclusively on finding ways to grow.
增长团队由公司不同部门的成员组成，它借助协作的力量，专门聚焦于寻找增长路径。
explain
Let's look at a real-world example.
让我们来看一个现实中的例子。
example
Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees working in the traditional departments of engineering, marketing and product development.
在成立增长团队之前，软件公司 BitTorrent 有50名员工，分别在工程、营销和产品开发等传统部门工作。
story
This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued.
这种组织方式一直带来不错的结果，直到2012年公司的增长陷入停滞。
contrast
The problem was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product.
问题在于，太多客户只使用其产品的基础免费版本。
explain
And despite improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.
而且，尽管付费高级版不断改进，真正升级的用户仍寥寥无几。
qualify
Things changed, however, when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard, created a growth team and sparked the kind of fresh perspective they needed.
然而，一位富有创新精神的项目营销经理加入后，情况发生了变化：他组建增长团队，并激发出了公司所需要的新鲜视角。
action_turn
By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the lack of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue.
当团队从营销角度审视工程问题时，便清楚地发现，升级不足并不是产品质量造成的。
explain
Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered.
大多数客户只是不了解高级版，也不知道它能提供什么。
conclude
Armed with this insight, the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently promoting the premium version to users of the free version.
有了这一洞见，营销和工程团队联手，通过向免费版用户醒目推广高级版来提高认知度。
sequence
As a result, upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.
结果，升级量猛增，收入提高了92%。
conclude
But in order for your growth team to succeed, it needs to have a strong leader.
不过，要让增长团队取得成功，就必须有一位强有力的负责人。
contrast
It needs someone who can unite the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement.
团队需要一个能够团结跨学科成员、让大家始终沿着改进方向前进的人。
explain
This leader will identify the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the accomplishment of these goals.
这位负责人要确定目标领域、设定清晰目标，并为目标的完成规定时间框架。
sequence
The growth leader is also responsible for keeping the team focused on moving forward and steering them clear of distractions.
增长团队负责人还要确保团队专注于向前推进，并使其远离干扰。
emphasize
While attractive, new ideas can be distracting; the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't serve the current goal and need to be put on the back burner.
新的想法虽然诱人，却也可能分散注意力；团队负责人必须判断这些想法何时无助于当前目标，并把它们暂时搁置。
warning

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 人造草坪的便利与生态代价
articles.context: 文章围绕英国园艺界对人造草坪的争议展开：皇家园艺学会因环境与生物多样性损害而抵制塑料草坪，支持者则强调天然草坪也有资源成本，政府目前倾向于依靠现有规则而非全面禁令。
rows: In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price.
为了追求完美草坪，全国各地的房主正在走一条捷径——而为此付出代价的却是环境。
advance
About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles.
每年约有800万平方米的塑料草坪被售出，但如今反对声已经蔓延到园艺界的最高层。
contrast
The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos.
切尔西花展已禁止在今年的活动中使用人造草坪，称其不符合花展的理念。
report
The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
主办这项伦敦西部年度花展的英国皇家园艺学会（RHS）表示，之所以实行禁令，是因为塑料草坪会损害环境和生物多样性。
explain
Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: “We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic.
RHS的埃德·霍恩说：“我们去年启动了可持续发展战略，而人造草坪与我们的理念以及我们对塑料的看法根本不一致。
dialogue
We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.”
我们建议使用真草，因为它具有环境效益，包括支持野生动物、缓解洪涝以及给环境降温。”
dialogue
The RHS’s decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes.
RHS作出这一决定之际，活动人士也在努力提高公众对人造草坪所带来问题的认识。
advance
A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers.
一个声称要“揭穿人造草坪绿色包装”的推特账号已经拥有2万多名关注者。
report
It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns.
该账号正鼓励人们签署两份请愿书：一份呼吁禁止销售塑料草坪，另一份呼吁对这类草坪征收“生态损害税”。
explain
They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.
两份请愿书分别收集到了7,276个和11,282个签名。
statistic
However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol.
然而，人造草坪的支持者指出，天然草坪同样会带来环境影响：它需要修剪，因此通常会消耗电力或汽油。
contrast
The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more.
该行业还指出，真草需要大量用水、除草剂或其他养护措施，而且铺设人造草坪的人往往会更频繁地使用花园。
explain
The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.
该行业还声称，铺设人造草坪的人平均会花500英镑购买花园里的树木或灌木，从而为昆虫提供栖息地。
report
In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has “no plans to ban the use of artificial grass”.
针对去年另一份要求禁止人造草坪、并收集到3万个签名的请愿书，政府回应称“没有计划禁止使用人造草坪”。
report
It added: “We prefer to help people and organisations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters.
政府补充说：“相比就此类问题立法，我们更愿意帮助个人和机构作出正确选择。
dialogue

However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives.”
不过，人造草坪的使用必须遵守现有的法律和政策保障措施，以保护生物多样性并确保可持续排水；与此同时，加强生物多样性责任等措施应当促使公共机构考虑可持续的替代方案。”
qualify_quote

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 美国国家公园真正缺的不是商业化，而是稳定资金
articles.context: 文章批评以私有化和商业化解决美国国家公园资金危机的思路，指出公园基础设施长期失修的根源是慢性资金不足，而公众愿意额外纳税维护公园，其生态、教育、历史与文化价值也远超商业收入。
rows: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks.
人们很容易把联邦政府为填补国家公园长期资金缺口而提出的设想斥为荒唐。
advance
Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
难道真有人认为，让亚马逊把包裹送到你在优胜美地的帐篷前，或者让餐车在红杉国家公园的巨杉下排成一列，是个好主意吗？
ask
But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis.
但有一点政府说对了：美国国家公园确实正陷入危机。
contrast
Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion.
这些公园累积的维护欠账超过120亿美元。
statistic
Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
道路、步道、洗手间、游客中心以及其他基础设施都在破败。
explain
But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all.
然而，把露营地私有化、商业化并不是包治百病的办法。
contrast
Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
露营地只占全部基础设施欠账中的很小一部分，而且园内企业平均仅把约5%的收入上交给国家公园管理局。
explain

Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
更重要的是，进一步私有化必然会削弱每年3亿游客来到国家公园的一个主要理由：享受自然，并暂时摆脱充斥日常生活的商业喧嚣。
warning
The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding.
真正的问题在于，这些公园长期资金不足。
emphasize
An economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact.
一项针对700名美国纳税人的经济调查发现，人们愿意支付一笔可观的钱，以确保国家公园及其项目完整保留下来。
report
Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
约81%的受访者表示，未来10年愿意缴纳额外税款，以避免国家公园遭到任何削减。
statistic
The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature.
国家公园既是人们逃离日常生活的去处，也是自然的象征，因此为美国居民提供了巨大价值。
advance

On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism.
除此之外，国家公园还通过广泛的教育项目、碳封存带来的积极气候影响、对文化艺术生活的贡献，以及旅游业创造价值。
explain
The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life.
国家公园还帮助保存美国的历史记忆，与全国数千个地方辖区合作保护历史遗址，让这些地方的故事重新鲜活起来。
explain
The parks do all this on a shoestring.
而国家公园完成这一切，靠的却是极其有限的预算。
emphasize
Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009.
国会每年只为国家公园系统拨款30亿美元——按通胀调整后的美元计算，除2009年一次性增加外，这一数额自2001年以来一直没有增长。
statistic
Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
与此同时，年游客人数自1980年以来增长了50%以上，如今已达到每年3.3亿人次。
contrast

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 互联网没有毁掉记忆，而是在改变我们记忆什么
articles.context: 文章讨论“认知卸载”：互联网使人更少记住可随时检索的事实、更多记住如何找到信息。研究者认为这未必意味着记忆退化，可能反而释放认知资源用于概念思考；现阶段仍缺乏证据证明互联网损害专注或记忆。
rows: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow.
哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝齐·斯帕罗认为，互联网改变的或许只是我们记住什么，而不是我们的记忆能力本身。
advance
In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain,” for example).
2011年，斯帕罗主持了一项研究，参与者被要求把40条零碎事实记录到电脑中，例如“鸵鸟的眼睛比它的大脑还大”。
story
Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved.
一半参与者被告知这些信息会被删除，另一半则被告知信息会被保存。
compare
Guess what?
结果如何呢？
ask
The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers.
后一组在之后接受测试时并没有努力回忆这些信息，因为他们知道可以从电脑中找到。
explain
In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in.
在同一项研究中，还有一组参与者被要求同时记住信息本身以及存放这些信息的文件夹。
sequence
They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders.
他们没有记住信息，却记住了如何找到那些文件夹。
contrast
In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.
换句话说，斯帕罗说，人类记忆并没有衰退，而是在“适应新的通信技术”。
conclude
In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading.”
从非常实际的意义上说，互联网正在成为我们记忆的外置硬盘，这一过程被称为“认知卸载”。
explain
Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans.
传统上，数据库、图书馆以及其他人承担着这一角色。
compare
Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance.
例如，你的父亲可能从不记生日，因为你的母亲会记得。
example
Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside.
有人担心这会对社会产生破坏性影响，但斯帕罗看到的却是积极的一面。
contrast

Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet.
她认为，也许这种趋势会改变我们的学习方式：从关注单个事实和死记硬背，转向更重视概念性思考——而后者并不是互联网能够直接提供的。
advance
“I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things,” Sparrow says, adding that we haven’t lost our ability to do it.
斯帕罗说：“就我个人而言，我从未觉得记住东西本身具有多大的智力价值。”她还补充说，我们并没有失去这种能力。
dialogue
Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains.
另一些专家则说，现在要弄清互联网如何影响大脑还为时过早。
qualify
There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons.
例如，心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·J·西蒙斯写道，目前没有实验证据表明互联网会妨碍我们的专注能力。
explain

And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.
而在2008年加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学与人类行为研究所一项有24名参与者的研究中，对熟悉电脑的老年人而言，上网比阅读更能调动大脑。
report

“There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I’d have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm.
心理学教授本杰明·斯托姆指出：“我们日益依赖互联网或许会付出一些代价，但我想，总体而言，它带来的好处会超过这些代价。”
qualify_quote
“It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better?
“看起来很明显，记忆正在发生变化，但这种变化是不是朝着更好的方向呢？
dialogue
At this point, we don’t know.”
目前，我们还不知道。”
settle

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 青少年的叛逆与利他为何会同时上升
articles.context: 文章以青少年“既叛逆又利他”的悖论为切口，介绍研究发现：亲社会行为与叛逆行为都在青春期上升并随后回落，二者可能共同受“奖励敏感性”驱动，尤其是对社会性奖励的敏感。
rows: Teenagers are paradoxical.
青少年充满矛盾。
advance
That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language.
这只是一种温和而疏离的说法，父母谈到同一件事时往往会用强烈得多的措辞。
playful
But the paradox is scientific as well as personal.
但这种矛盾不仅是个人体验，也是一个科学现象。
contrast
In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other.
进入青春期后，那些过去几乎事事依赖成年人的无助孩子，会逐渐成为能够照顾自己并互相帮助的独立个体。
explain
At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.
与此同时，曾经快乐听话的孩子也会变成叛逆、爱冒险的青少年。
contrast
A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand.
莱顿大学的埃弗琳·克罗恩及其同事在《儿童发展》期刊发表的一项新研究表明，青少年的积极面与消极面往往相伴而生。
report
The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence.
这项研究属于近年来重新认识青春期的一股新思潮。
advance
For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved.
长期以来，科学家和政策制定者都把注意力集中在一种观念上：青少年是一个需要解决的问题。
story
The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.
新的研究则强调，青春期既是风险期，也是机遇期。
contrast
The researchers studied “prosocial” and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old.
研究人员考察了200多名11至28岁的儿童和年轻人的“亲社会”特征与叛逆特征。
report

The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.
参与者填写问卷，报告自己多常做利他、积极的事情，例如牺牲自己的利益帮助朋友；以及多常做叛逆、消极的事情，例如醉酒或很晚不归。
explain
Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older.
其他研究已经表明，叛逆行为会随着进入青春期而增加，之后又随着年龄增长而逐渐减弱。
sequence
But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior.
但有趣的是，新研究显示，亲社会行为也遵循同样的模式。
contrast
Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly helping a friend.
与更小的孩子或成年人相比，青少年更可能报告自己做过无私帮助朋友之类的事情。
report
Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness.
最重要的是，亲社会性与叛逆性之间存在正相关。
emphasize
The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others.
越叛逆的青少年，往往也越可能帮助别人。
explain
The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.
青春期所谓“好”的一面和“坏”的一面，似乎是共同发展的。
conclude
Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments?
这些看似矛盾的发展背后，是否存在某个共同因素？
ask
One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call “reward sensitivity.”
一种观点认为，青少年的行为与研究者所谓的“奖励敏感性”有关。
explain
Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs.
决策总是在奖励与风险、收益与代价之间进行权衡。
compare
“Reward sensitivity” measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.
“奖励敏感性”衡量的是，需要多大的奖励才能抵消风险。
explain
Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you.
青少年尤其容易受到社会性奖励的影响——赢得比赛、给新朋友留下印象、让那个男孩注意到你。
example
Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age.
奖励敏感性与亲社会行为、冒险行为一样，似乎都会在青春期上升，之后随着年龄增长再次下降。
conclude
Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.
不知为何，当你到了30岁，派对上可能发生的新鲜刺激之事，似乎就不再值得你为此从沙发上起身了。
playful

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 英国净零建筑新规为何短期推高住房与扩建成本
articles.context: 文章介绍英国英格兰地区为实现2050净零排放而实施的新建筑法规。新规提高通风、能效、供暖、门窗和玻璃面积等标准，短期会增加材料与施工成本，但业内人士预计规模化后成本会回落，长期可通过节能收益回补。
rows: Net-Zero Rules Set to Send Cost of New Homes and Extensions Soaring
净零新规将使新建住房和扩建工程成本飙升
advance
New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones.
旨在提高能源效率的新建筑法规将推高新建住房的价格，也会增加现有住宅扩建和阁楼改造的费用。
advance
The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050.
这些规则于周三在英格兰生效，是英国政府到2050年把碳排放降至净零计划的一部分。
report
They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles.
新规为通风、能源效率和供暖设定了新标准，并规定新建住宅必须配备电动汽车充电点。
explain

The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs are already driving up bills.
这些措施是多年来建筑法规最重大的变化；业内专家表示，在材料短缺和高人工成本已经推高账单之际，新规必然会进一步抬高价格。
warning
Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed.
建筑大师联合会首席执行官布赖恩·贝里表示，这些措施将要求采用新的材料、测试方法、产品和系统。
report
“All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high.
“在价格本已高得惊人的时候，这一切都会带来额外成本。
dialogue
Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more,” he says.
消费者不可避免地要付更多钱。”他说。
dialogue
Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected.
测量师事务所 Naismiths 的加雷思·贝尔沙姆说，升级或扩建住宅的人会直接受到影响。
report
“The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation,” he explains.
他解释说：“最大的变化与供暖和保温有关。”
dialogue
“There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated.”
“扩建工程中使用多少玻璃有了新规定，而且任何新窗户或新门都必须具有很高的保温性能。”
dialogue
Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun.
门窗必须符合更高标准，同时为减少来自阳光的不必要热量，玻璃面积也有了新的限制。
explain
Thomas Goodman, of MyJobQuote, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions.
MyJobQuote 的托马斯·古德曼说，这将给住宅扩建带来新的限制。
report
“Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss,” he says.
他说：“为了防止热量流失，窗户、门和屋顶采光窗的玻璃面积不得超过楼面面积的25%。”
dialogue
As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline.
由于新规于上周三生效，房地产开发商在截止日期前争相提交方案。
story
Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year.
在那一日期之前提交的任何方案都按旧规处理，只要工程在明年6月15日前开工，就可以继续推进。
explain
Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator.
Build Aviator 的马库斯·杰福德说，那些已经给项目核算成本、但尚未提交文件的建筑商，可能需要重新提交新的报价。
report
Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years.
过去两年，材料价格已经上涨了25%。
statistic
How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear.
新规究竟会使总体价格上涨多少，目前还不清楚。
qualify

“Whilst admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership,” says Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers.
全国购房者协会的乔纳森·罗兰德说：“这些规定的初衷虽然值得赞许，但在许多人已经觉得房价高到无法置业之际，它们还会进一步增加建房成本。”
evaluation_quote
“An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs.”
“由于新规，一项普通扩建工程可能会增加约3,000英镑的成本。”
dialogue
John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down.
Freeths 律师事务所的建筑律师约翰·凯利认为，价格最终会降下来。
report
But not in the immediate future.
但不会是在短期内。
contrast

“As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition,” he says.
他说：“随着市场适应新的要求以及支撑这些要求的技术，这些技术实现规模化后最终会降低成本；但短期内，我们都必须为这场必要的转型付出代价。”
qualify_quote
However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects.
不过，PRP 建筑事务所的安德鲁·梅勒补充说，从长期看，这些变化会带来更舒适、更节能的住宅。
contrast
“Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings.
“房主很可能会随着时间推移，通过节省能源账单把这部分成本赚回来。
dialogue
It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time.”
眼下情况显然会很不稳定，但从长远来看，他们会获得这种收益。”
settle

articles.title: 翻译 · 诗歌的力量、起源与朗诵传统
articles.context: 短文以华兹华斯和浪漫主义开篇，说明诗歌凭借词语、节奏与声音改变读者感受；诗歌早于文字而存在，长期承担讲故事和传承历史的功能，并天然与歌曲和朗诵相连。
rows: In the late 18th century, William Wordsworth became famous for his poems about nature.
18世纪末，威廉·华兹华斯因描写自然的诗歌而闻名。
story
And he was one of the founders of a movement called Romanticism, which celebrated the wonders of the natural world.
他也是浪漫主义运动的奠基者之一，这场运动赞颂自然世界的奇迹。
explain
Poetry is powerful.
诗歌富有强大的感染力。
emphasize
Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently.
诗歌的能量和韵律能够抓住读者，把他们带往另一个世界，并让他们以不同的方式看待事物。
explain
Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring.
借助精心选择的词语和短语，诗歌可以富有戏剧性、幽默、优美、动人而又鼓舞人心。
explain
No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write.
没有人确切知道诗歌始于何时，但它已经存在了数千年，甚至早在人们会书写之前就已出现。
advance
It was a way to tell stories and pass down history.
它曾是一种讲述故事、传承历史的方式。
explain
It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud.
诗歌与歌曲关系密切，即使被写下来，通常也是为了大声吟诵而创作。
explain
Poems really come to life when they are recited.
诗歌在被朗诵时才真正鲜活起来。
emphasize
This can also help with understanding them too, because the rhythm and sounds of the words become clearer.
朗诵也有助于理解诗歌，因为词语的韵律与声音会因此变得更加清晰。
conclude
